alex: Quick follow-up to the offload RFC — thinking about a tenant‑fair probabilistic evictor that uses a monotonic spline to map hotness -> eviction probability. Sketching tradeoffs here.

morgan: TL;DR please.

alex: TL;DR: avoid hard watermarks. compute continuous hotness H per allocation (recency + frequency + size penalty). feed H into a calibrated spline that outputs P_evict in [0,1]. soft decisions reduce synchronized thrash and let small noisy tenants yield to steady heavy tenants.

sam: Where does this live? runtime evictor vs offload controller?

alex: Runtime evictor, coexists with existing watermark-based path. Probabilistic path is used when global pressure is moderate; under emergency OOM we keep deterministic sweep.

taylor: Major concerns: CPU overhead on hot path and repeat evict-reload loops.

alex: Mitigations: (1) cheap counters on access (u8 saturating), (2) sampled full score updates in epoch ticks, (3) sticky cooldown after evict to avoid immediate re-pull.

kai: How compute H exactly? we need something stable and explainable for SRE.

alex: Proposal: H = sigmoid( w_r * recency_norm + w_f * freq_norm - w_s * log(size) ) where recency_norm is decayed accesses in last Nms and freq_norm is rolling hits. Then apply monotonic spline S so P_evict = S(H) * pressure_scale.

morgan: Can you show minimal pseudocode?

alex: ```
// per allocation metadata (8 bytes)
struct Meta { u8 recency; u8 freq; u16 last_epoch; u32 cool_until; }

on_access(meta) { if (fast_path_sample()) meta.recency = min(255, meta.recency + REC_INC); if (fast_path_sample()) meta.freq = min(255, meta.freq + FREQ_INC); }

compute_score(meta) { r = decay(meta.recency); f = meta.freq; h = wr*r + wf*f - ws * log(size); return clamp(h, 0.0, 1.0); }

maybe_evict(meta) { h = compute_score(meta); p = spline_lookup(h); if (rand01() < p) evict(); }
```

sam: That keeps per-access cheap. Cooldown via meta.cool_until helps.

taylor: We also need a clear API for tenant weighting. How do we set fairness?

alex: Tenants get weight w_i (quota + SLA weight). We scale H by 1/w_i or multiply P_evict by (base_weight / w_i). In practice: P_evict = base_p * (W_avg / w_i).

kai: Danger: tiny tenants could be starved if weights misconfigured. We should clamp scaling to [0.25, 4.0].

morgan: Telemetry plan? important to detect regressions.

alex: Telemetry: per-tenant counters: evicts, re-fetches (post-evict misses), avg latency pre/post evict, memory residency, and churn-rate. We'll add a small eval harness that replays production traces and measures tail latency & token cost.

sam: Fallback/rollout strategy? we can't risk mass regressions.

alex: Canary rollout on 5% of traffic (dedicated tenants + small public canary). Gate by two metrics: 95p latency delta < 5% AND post-evict miss-rate change < 10%. If breached, automatic revert.

taylor: Implementation owner? timeline?

alex: I'll own the prototype. Plan: 2w spike to get perf numbers + perf job. taylor owns production rollout automation and cooldown policy. sam will help on telemetry + trace replay.

morgan: One more thing — cost model: we need to show unit-token saving vs CPU cost. Add small microbench.

alex: Yep, perf job will include cost estimate (GPU token-savings from reduced KV rehydration vs CPU cycles on evictor).

kai: Ops question: how do we expose knobs? runtime flags? console?

alex: Runtime flags for canary and thresholds. Expose sanitized knobs in Console: tenant weight override, canary toggle, telemetry retention for evict stats.

morgan: sgtm. Please add an RFC follow-up doc with checklist items.

alex: Will do. Creating follow-up doc: rfc-evict-spline-prototype.md and a perf job. @deploy-bot can you create a tracking ticket?

deploy-bot: Created ticket INF-4281: "probabilistic-evictor-spline-prototype". assignees: alex,taylor,sam.

alex: Next action items I have recorded: 1) prototype + perf harness (alex) 2) telemetry + dashboards (sam) 3) canary automation + cooldowns (taylor) 4) RFC follow-up doc (alex).

morgan: Thanks — excited to see numbers. :thumbsup:
